sadness: Say it once, out loud, even if your voice is flat. You are not required to feel better first.
anxiety: Say it slowly enough to hear the words. If your mind wanders, start the line again.
fear: Say it where you are, before you move. Fear does not have to be gone for the words to be true.
anger: Before anything else, stop talking. Say this instead, and deal with the matter later.
loneliness: Say it aloud in an empty room. Then message one person, about anything.
despair: Say the first line only, if that is all you can manage. That counts.
overwhelm: Put one thing down before you say this. Choose the thing, then say it.
gratitude: Say it before the feeling passes. Naming what happened is the point.
envy: Say it, then make one quiet duʿā for the person you are thinking of.
shame: Say it without adding a promise you are not sure you can keep.
distress: Say it as it is, without arranging your words first.
illness: Say it where you are resting. It is not instead of treatment.
someone-ill: Say it by their side if you can, quietly enough not to alarm them.
death: Say it when the words will come. There is no window you have missed.
debt: Say it, then write down what you owe. Both are part of the same turning.
poverty: Say it, then do the next practical thing you had been avoiding.
oppression: Say it. Being wronged does not oblige you to stay where you are.
enemy: Say it without naming them out loud, if naming them makes it worse.
failure: Say it before you explain it to anyone. The explanation can wait.
marriage: Say it for them by name, privately, before you raise anything with them.
children: Say it over them while they sleep, or from the next room.
parents: Say it, then call them if you still can.
reconcile: Say it, then send the shorter message rather than the fuller one.
knowledge: Say it before you open the book, not instead of opening it.
work: Say it at the start, then do the work.
decision: Say it, then leave the decision for one night before acting.
travel: Say it as you set out, not once you have arrived.
forgiveness: Say it in your own words after, if you have words of your own.
weak-iman: Say it on a day you do not feel like it. Those are the days it is for.
waswas: Say it once and move. Repeating it to feel certain is the thing itself.
steadfastness: Say it, then do the smallest version of the thing you keep abandoning.
death-remembrance: Say it, then settle one thing you have been leaving unsettled.
refuge: Say it before you need it, so it is there when you do.
evil-eye: Say it, then leave it. Watching for signs is its own harm.
home: Say it as you come through the door, before you say anything else.
morning-evening: Say it with the first cup of the day, so it has somewhere to live.
sleep: Say it lying down, phone already face down.
eating: Say it before the first mouthful, not after you remember.
prayer: Say it in its place in the prayer, not as an extra.
mosque: Say it at the door, going in and coming out.
rain-weather: Say it while it is still falling.
dhikr: Say it while your hands are busy with something else.
misc: Say it once, and let that be enough for today.
intimacy: Said once, before, and quietly. Nothing else is asked of you, and it is not a test you can fail.
desire: Say it when the pull starts rather than after it has passed. If it has already passed, seeking forgiveness is its own door and nobody is counting how many times you have used it.
